sources.title: Steam can now show game achievements in separate ‘sets’
sources.text: Developers with games on Steam can split achievements from a base game and its DLC into sets with their own progress bars. Developers with games on Steam can split achievements from a base game and its DLC into sets with their own progress bars. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Valve is introducing a major new feature for Steam achievements called “achievement sets” that lets developers list different groups of achievements for a base game and DLCs. “In games that support sets, you still unlock achievements by playing the game as usual,” Valve says . “But when you browse what you have unlocked afterward, Steam will break the long list of game achievements into the developer-created sets, making it easier to see what you have completed and to find other related achievements you can unlock next.” Achievement sets have their own progress bars, and if you finish a set, you’ll get a “set complete” trophy that’s visible on your profile. Steam will support seasonal achievement sets that developers can archive, too. “We think there are a lot of fun ways games can take advantage of the temporary nature this can add, such as adding achievements to season-based games or enabling time-limited holiday achievements,” Valve says. A handful of games already support achievement sets, per Valve: The company is also refreshing the Steam Achievements page to show “a summary of your overall progress, progress in each achievement set, and details on individual achievements.” The new achievements features are available in the latest Steam client beta, Valve says .

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Steam achievements are getting a huge overhaul, with separate sets for DLC and season passes, and an easy way to compare with friends
sources.text: It's in beta now, but will likely release widely in about a month. Valve has pushed a new update to its Steam client beta introducing big changes to how achievements work and how they're displayed. Developers can now create sets of achievements customized to their game, like mastering a specific character class or finishing a singleplayer campaign. Sets also distinguish base game achievements from separate DLC and seasonal sets. Previously if you unlocked all achievements for a game you'd see a nice 'n' tidy 100% in your achievements list. But if that game got DLC with new achievements, that 100% would drop accordingly. I can understand why achievement heads would be annoyed by this: what if you have no intention of playing the DLC, but want to retain 100% completion bragging rights? This update fixes that, assuming devs use it. It's a similar situation for seasonal achievements, which I can see working well with battle passes. The example Valve uses is a set called "Halloween Event Achievements" which are valid for a certain period and don't affect the achievement count of the base game. In other words: if you have the completionist itch but skip a season, it won't affect your base game stats. All these changes have prompted a refresh of the achievements page. Most achievements info is now displayed on a single page: your progress towards overall completion, and your progress towards unlocking individual achievements. I especially like that you can now directly compare achievements with up to three friends at once, which is what's being displayed at the bottom of the above image. This has been a feature on PlayStation consoles for a while, and so has separate sets for DLC achievements. It's nice that Valve has caught up. Naturally, not every game on Steam will have implemented this new system yet, but the following games have: This system is still in beta, but you can sign up for the Client Beta or just wait: as we saw with Steam's new screensaver feature , betas normally only last around a month. sources.title: Steam Achievements Overhaul Now Available in Beta
sources.text: A new update has arrived in Steam Beta, overhauling the platform’s Achievements system and adding new Achievement Sets. Steam has recognized that games live longer thanks to DLCs and expansions, and while that’s great for gamers, it can sometimes mess up the platform’s achievement tracking and even remove players from completion status. Hence, the DLCs will no longer impact 100% completion, and the achievements have been compartmentalized into new ‘Achievement Sets’. Achievement Sets is a new system that has arrived with Steam Beta and is now available for a select set of games. With the new system, developers can compartmentalize a game’s achievements into different sets and define each one’s purpose. For example, a game could have different sets for single-player, multiplayer, DLC, and more. The new system doesn’t change how you earn achievements; you still earn them by playing the game. What’s changed is the viewing experience, with the long list now segregated into different sets with their own progress bar. Players will also earn a new “set complete” trophy when they unlock every achievement in a set. With new DLCs and expansions, developers can add new achievement sets specific to that content without affecting players’ progress. Steam has revealed different achievement sets: Base Game and DLC. Base game sets can be earned by playing the game, and this progress is shown in blue on the page. You can only access DLC achievement sets when you purchase that content; progress for these sets is shown in purple. The new system also lets developers add temporary sets for season-based games or time-limited holiday achievements. Once that time period is over, the developers can archive this set, and only the users who have unlocked the achievements or the set can showcase it on their profile. The overhaul also adds an updated Achievements page on Steam, accessible from the Games List on the web and from games in your Steam Library. The updated page will now display a summary of the player’s overall progress, the progress for each achievement set of that game, and details on individual achievements. Players can also toggle Global Stats or per-achievement completion rates on the same page. Additionally, Search has been expanded with new filters for achievement sets and for locked or unlocked achievements. Players will also be able to compare their game progress with up to three friends, including rare achievements, completed sets, and DLC sets. Along with all of these changes, there are some other enhancements as well: Currently, Steam’s Achievement Sets are only available to players and developers in beta . sources.text: Developer The Third One has dropped its first trailer for its new project, Angelfall. Let me tell you, there’s nothing angelic about the Archdemon you control, as you tear through humans and harvest souls. Angelfall is a new ‘roguelike reverse-horror game,’ where you fight hundreds of enemies at once. The visuals are dark and grizzly, in keeping with the game’s theme, and did I mention its pounding heavy metal soundtrack that would give Mick Gordon a run for his money? There’s so much going on at once in Angelfall that it’s easily the kind of game you could kick back with a cold drink and watch someone else play and have a great time. Absolute cinema, some would say. You need to use your Archdemon’s range of weapons and abilities to conquer perilously large mobs and take down bosses, while enjoying an industrial breakdown or two. The game can be wishlisted now, and there’s even a free Angelfall Steam demo for you to try out. Here’s the official game description to get you hyped: ‘Face the endless armies of Light and become the nightmare they fear! Angelfall is a roguelike reverse-horror game, in which you play as powerful Archdemon, slaughter hordes of humans and holy warriors, harvest their souls, and discover devastating synergies. Grow stronger, unlock new powers, and conquer the Light.’ Still not hyped enough? Check out the full gameplay trailer. How good does Angelfall look? Are you gonna try out the free demo? The odds might be stacked against you but with awesome powers, a winning personality and up to four-player local co-up on your side, the Smogulan Empire’s days are numbered! stories.summary: Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Sega and Creative Assembly remove Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale as it "falls short of both your expectations and our own standards"
sources.text: Recently launched title has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam, with players citing AI upscaling and performance issues Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Since its October 13 launch, the remaster has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam. Players have reported that assets such as unit cards and new cutscenes display AI-generated features , including extra fingers and armor merging into characters' bodies. As described on Steam , the "underlying graphics technology has been brought to modern standards to take advantage of new methods in rendering," resulting in improved graphics and textures. In response, both companies issued a joint statement acknowledging that the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards." "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be." "As a result we are working with platform holders to temporarily remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game." "We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War." Earlier this year, Sega faced criticism for its use of generative AI in Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The game's Steam page included a generative AI disclaimer, which clarified that Sega uses the technology "as a support tool for developers, aiming to provide better content to our users and enable developers to focus more on creative tasks." "We have used such generative AI support tools during development of Crazy Taxi: World Tour. No AI was used in reference to the performers in game." In a statement to Game Informer , Sega clarified that generative AI was "used to support our teams during the development of background assets" and that "assets generated were still subject to review by the development team."

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: The Shogun 2 remaster is so bad, Sega is removing it from sale and bringing back the original
sources.text: Sega admits Shogun 2 - Complete Edition "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," so it's going back to the drawing board. Just two days after the disastrous release of Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition, Sega says it is removing the game from sale and putting the original back until it gets things sorted out. Which brings us to now: After two days of silence, Sega has finally made a move: It says "the current experience is not where it needs to be," and is thus "working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues." Anyone who purchased Shogun 2 - Complete Edition will still have access to it, but how (or if) Sega will enable them to go back to playing the original version wasn't clarified. Pulling Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and restoring the original is obviously the right move, and today's message promises improvements to the game to bring it more in-line with expectations, so hopefully we'll see some of the more glaring bugs and QoL issues resolved. But all of this is still a very bad look for Creative Assembly, which has had something of an up-and-down history with its games and players over the years. It's a particular shame coming so soon after the company's successful launch of the Lords of the End Times expansion for Total War: Warhammer, which has been widely praised. The announcement of Total War: Warhammer 40k also has a lot of RTS fans, and WH40K sickos, very excited, and nonsense like this really takes the wind out of those sails: If Shogun 2 - Complete Edition allowed out the door in this condition, how are fans supposed to expect better in the future? A few fans have also pointed out that in 2024, Sega's Aegis-CWA union accused the company of outsourcing Q&A and some localization services, resulting in the layoffs of 61 people. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. As I write this, Shogun 2 - Complete Edition remains available for purchase on Steam , GOG , and the Epic Games Store —Sega has not specified when it will be removed. Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Complete Edition , a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including “improved visuals,” “1440p and 4K UI scaling,” and modernized controls. It has an “Overwhelmingly Negative” rating on Steam , where it has already been pulled, and posts on Reddit showcase artwork that users believe AI messed up. “We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Sega and developer Creative Assembly wrote in a post . “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” The two companies say they will “reinstate the original game,” and existing owners will “still be able to access ” Complete Edition . Sega and Creative Assembly say that they are “working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 - Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” A studio called Mataboo is also listed as a developer for the game on Steam, and Mataboo highlights its work on the game on its website .

sources.title: Big Walk skipped Xbox to boycott Microsoft’s involvement with Israel
sources.text: ‘We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world.’﻿ ‘We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world.’﻿ If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Big Walk ’s co-op multiplayer walking adventure has proved popular since launching in August, but Xbox players have been excluded from the fun — and now the game’s creators have explained why. Developer House House said in a blog post that it decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which has called to boycott Microsoft, including products under the company’s gaming division. Microsoft was named a priority BDS target in June last year over contracts it has with the Israeli military and government , with the boycott specifically calling out Xbox consoles and Game Pass subscriptions, gaming franchises owned by Microsoft, and any gaming accessories produced by the company. Microsoft’s involvement with Israel has also been protested by its own employees , and the company has fired staffers for participating in pro-Palestine demonstrations. Here’s what House House said regarding its participation in the boycott: It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions. This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too. We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets. We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free. Big Walk is playable on Microsoft’s Windows operating system, however, as it’s available to download via Steam . We’ve asked House House why it hasn’t excluded Big Walk from Windows and will update if we hear back.

stories.title: Apparent Leaked Footage Shows Canceled Assassin's Creed Game Set in Qin Dynasty China
stories.summary: Ubisoft was apparently making another Assassin’s Creed game set in ancient China, except this one was a full-fat AC with a massive open world and a fancy umbrella weapon.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Apparent Leaked Footage Shows Canceled Assassin's Creed Game Set in Qin Dynasty China
sources.text: Ubisoft was apparently making another Assassin’s Creed game set in ancient China, except this one was a full-fat AC with a massive open world and a fancy umbrella weapon. According to a new report, the game was called Assassin’s Creed Destiny. Assassin’s Creed Jade will explore the same setting, targeting mobile. Destiny’s prototype footage appears to be aimed at modern consoles and PC instead. Destiny was reportedly set during 206 BCE, where the Qin dynasty made way for the Han dynasty after a brutal civil war. The game likely would have focused on Liu Bang’s rise to power. MP1st found the footage in developer portfolios. According to the report, the game was supposed to be a partnership between Ubisoft and Tencent, the Chinese conglomerate that owns huge portions of the games industry, including a 25% stake in Vantage Studios, a subsidiary that oversees some of Ubisoft’s biggest IPs. The footage shows a hooded assassin battling through a siege headed up by warlord Xiang Yu, before switching to greybox testing environments for combat abilities. There’s a spinning umbrella weapon shown at one point. Another snippet suggests players would have been able to choose between a male and female character, or it could have done the Shadows thing of having dual protagonists. Yin-yangs and ink brushes are used to tie the UI into the setting thematically. While Destiny was seemingly cancelled, Assassin’s Creed Jade is still in development. The last we heard about it was that it was delayed to 2025 . Considering it’s 2026 now, it’s probably safe to assume they’re having some issues getting the mobile game off the ground, which is ironic for a series about assassins who love rooftops. Elsewhere in the world of hidden blades, leaps of faith, and stylish hoods, Assassin’s Creed Hexe is the next major game in the series. If leaks are to be believed, that’s got its own development issues, mind you. One report suggests Assassin’s Creed Hexe developers decided to rework the game, removing magical abilities from the mix. Hexe's game director Benoit Richer recently departed the project for reasons unknown. That departure followed the exit of Clint Hocking, Hexe's creative director , sparking the beginning of a major internal reshuffle at the top of the franchise that saw Ubisoft veteran Jean Guesdon ascend to become Assassin's Creed Head of Content. Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: We finally get to see the canceled Assassin's Creed game set in China, and it looks pretty good
sources.text: Ubisoft and Tencent were making it together Any franchise that lasts a number of years always winds up with a few unrealized projects, whether from partnerships that fell through or ideas that simply just didn't come together. Assassin's Creed has a bunch of them, and details and footage of another one have emerged. This particular game was called Assassin's Creed Destiny, and it was part of a collaboration between Ubisoft and Chinese conglomerate Tencent . You might be aware these industry giants are currently working on Assassin's Creed Jade, a mobile game first announced back in 2022. They had a couple of other potential releases on the docket as well, and one of them was remarkably similar to Jade. In fact, according to details gleaned by MP1st , Assassin's Creed Destiny was also set in China, and during the same period, taking place around 206 BCE, nine years after the events of Jade. It would've been a full, triple-A game on modern hardware, marking a grand return to Chinese history after Assassin's Creed Chronicles way back in 2015. Jade is still fulfilling that promise, but on a different scale. Destiny was being handled by TiMi group, and we now have a smattering of images and clips demonstrating what could've been. This definitely looks like a full-on Assassin's Creed game. You've the player character skulking around a palace during the Qin Empire. Your mission is to prevent an invading army from stealing some form of treasure. Doing so gets bloodier and messier than anyone would like, but you spend the majority of your time in the shadows, taking out soldiers and other enemies. It looks intriguing - the architectural layouts offer plenty of exploration and the swords and spears make combat feel weighty. There's a spinning blade, somewhat like an umbrella, that seems like it would've been very entertaining. Destiny was only canceled last year, a casualty of restructuring at TiMi. It's unknown how far along the game ultimately was, or if any of its ideas live on in Jade. There's no release window for the mobile game yet, but at least we can now look at what could've been. sources.title: Shrek 2 Remastered Appears Briefly on XBOX Store
sources.text: It seems like XBOX accidentally posted a store listing for Shrek 2 Remastered early, and it has now been removed. Also, a GTA 6-inspired trailer for the game has appeared online. For those unaware, a massive Steam leak took place last month, where the platform’s API became accessible and discoverable. The leak ending up revealing a whole bunch of titles, including the Shrek 2 Remastered. Just a month later, an XBOX listing has solidified the existence of this game. The XBOX Store listing for Shrek 2 Remastered revealed all the new features for the title. First and foremost, the game has been rebuilt with 4K resolution, better textures, and an improved UI. It also adds a new Photo Mode and a Cheat Mode. The multiplayer stuff has been upgraded to include up to 4-player couch co-op, online, or mixed gameplay. Furthermore, players will be able to freely swap heroes while battling tons of enemies and bosses and solving puzzles. Interestingly, that’s not all that players have been informed about today regarding Shrek 2 Remastered. An announcement trailer (thanks, NotPaloIntel ) has surfaced online, and it’s inspired by the most anticipated game of the year, GTA 6. The start completely replicates the Rockstar art style, even the colors and the fonts, before the trailer eventually showcases different gameplay sections with upgraded visuals and much more. Additionally, the trailer ends with only XBOX Series X/S mentioned as the platform. sources.title: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 review
sources.text: Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware. The Asus ROG 20th anniversary lineup has been interesting. Black, gold, and indulgent feels like the tagline here, with the Azoth Extreme Edition 20 and ROG Harpe II Extreme Edition 20 containing actual gold, and a fitting price tag to boot. For any criticisms I may have, I don't think you're paying primarily for the branding on the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20, though. You get a new OLED screen which is bigger and brighter than the IPS panel in the standard Xbox Ally X, TMR thumbsticks, refined triggers, a new cooling system, and with that screen comes a snappy 0.2 ms response time. Refined is a good word for the device as a whole. Coming a year later than the last model, the software is smooth and intuitive, and it's easy to swap between Xbox and Windows mode, though it still doesn't feel like a console in practice. For my money, it's the best ROG Ally on the market right now, but the memory crisis has skewed the price of all gaming gear, and the X20 is certainly not the best value as a result. ✅ You want a beefy OLED handheld: OLED handhelds are still fairly niche, and with recent price bumps, I'd pick this over the Legion Go 2 or OneXPlayer's offerings. ✅ You want power on the go: I'd suggest a significantly cheaper handheld if you are after low-intensity games and don't particularly care for big-budget ones. For your Cyberpunks and your Horizons, you will want a Z2 Extreme chip or better to play them at a decent resolution and settings. ❌ You're fine with IPS: $300 more for the X20 over the X is pretty steep, especially if you aren't dying to play on an OLED. ❌ You live in the UK: The pricing on the X20 is not as good value in Britain, with the superior G3-equipped MSI Claw being only £100 more (though no OLED) and the standard Xbox Ally X £400 less. Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 (or should I say XBOX) is a relatively granular update on the Xbox Ally X . I noticed it immediately when putting the two devices side by side, but when it comes to performance, you're getting identical experiences. They have the same chip, the same memory, the same storage. That's the Ryzen Z2 Extreme, 24 GB LPDDR5X, and 1 TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 2280, respectively. Given you don't get a performance bump, you've gotta really care about the details to consider the X20. Arguably its biggest upgrade is the OLED panel, and it is a beauty. The DisplayHDR True Black 1400 certification isn't just for show, as it pops, appearing both bright and ultra-vibrant. It's also got a bigger screen, which does make the device more immersive, but also larger and chunkier. You can technically upgrade the plain old joysticks in the ROG Xbox Ally X with a TMR module with a bit of know-how, but slapping in your own OLED screen would be very difficult, and I certainly wouldn't trust myself to do such fine electronic surgery. Therefore, I do see value in an upgraded, refined, and pretty older brother of last year's device. It's also got a whole new cooling system for frostier temps. You also get smaller upgrades here, like the ability to pull up and turn the D-Pad to make the corner buttons more or less pronounced, plus greater grooves on the face buttons to stop jagged edges, and a combination of more clicky bumpers and smoother triggers. These all combine to make the X20 feel more thoughtful in approach, and given the price bump, it sort of has to do that. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products The X20 doesn't come with a charger in the box, which makes sense from an e-waste point of view, but it does mean you will get lacking plugged-in performance without an appropriately speedy charger. For instance, I ran the device at 35 W mode and did some of my benchmarks before realising I wasn't getting the full-fat 35 W mode because my charger wasn't quick enough. Could you say that's my fault for not seeing the low-power pop-up from Asus' software Armoury Crate? Absolutely. Does that mean you may need to pick up a quick charger if you want full-wattage plugged-in performance? Also, absolutely. The box for the X20 also comes with a cardboard stand, which doesn't feel as luxurious as the device itself but is clean, effective, and environmentally conscious. It's a small but decent addition that I've been using consistently since unboxing the device without any problems. There was a brief period when the original Asus ROG Xbox Ally X was the highest-performing gaming handheld money could buy. That was until the launch of the much more expensive MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ CG3EM (catchy name, I know) broke onto the scene. Despite launching a year after the original Xbox Ally X, the X20 sees no difference in power (as it has identical specs), and therefore my performance figures are more or less the same as what Dave got in his review of the standard Xbox Ally X. I got a little less in Metro and a little more in Horizon and Cyberpunk 2077, with lower 1% lows in F1 25. In a handful of games, with upscaling on and off (35 W plugged in) I left the GPU memory budget at 8 GB, flicked the device onto its 35 W Turbo mode, and had a good time in F1 24, Horizon Zero Dawn, and Metro Exodus without any upscaling. sources.title: Xbox Ally X 20 vs Xbox Ally X: A wickedly bright OLED screen and frosty temps make for a begrudgingly attractive upgrade for the Asus handheld
sources.text: All that glitters might actually be gold. So, you've seen the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 in all its black and gold glory and wondered if it's worth paying $300 more for it. Well, the answer is 'it really depends on what kind of device you are looking for' and 'how much is a fresh OLED screen worth to you?' Unlike the other ROG 20th anniversary edition bits of Asus gear, the X20 is not about superfluous add-ons (unless you pick up the bundle with XR glasses). You aren't getting a commemorative faceplate here, or extra stickers. You get an OLED screen, TMR thumbsticks, improved thermals, and MicroSD Express compatibility. You also get Impulse triggers, which means they can rumble independently, and the D-Pad can be flicked around to make the corners more or less pronounced. The screen is perhaps the biggest sell here, with its 1400 HDR-certified display going up to a peak brightness of 1,400 nits. As I found in my review , it's so sizzlingly bright at points that I looked at the sun in Cyberpunk 2077 while lying in bed one night and actually winced. Check out the full differences below. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible In a handful of games and productivity apps (35 W plugged in) With both devices featuring the same chip and memory, you can expect more or less the same performance. In my testing, I got lower Metro performance and worse 1% lows in F1 25, but better performance in Horizon Zero Dawn, Cyberpunk 2077 and 3DMark, so the framerate differences overall just about balance out. I also noticed the X20 never went above 49 watts, which means I would feel more comfortable cranking up the wattage. It helps that its thermals are much improved. Recorded in HW Info whilst performing gaming benchmarks (35 W plugged in) The X20 comes with a refined new thermal cooling system, and it's more than just a marketing term. I recorded temps up to 17 °C cooler compared to the previous model, and even in long gaming sessions, I couldn't manage to push the system's temp above 80°C with its included wattage modes (between 17 W and 35 W). Importantly, I never felt that heat on my fingers as I played, making it a relatively frosty gaming device. Recorded using PCMark 10's gaming battery life test (25 W) In stress testing gaming benchmarks, the X20 managed 2 hours and 9 minutes in the 25 W gaming mode, and almost 3 hours in the 17 W mode. Importantly, it can get up to 9 hours of indie gaming on the go, in my experience. The standard X model has the exact same size battery, so you can expect a similar battery life, though our testing saw it perform a little under the X20. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products Though you're getting similar performance figures, the day-to-day use of the Ally X20 is superior from my experience. The screen is gorgeous and super bright, all the buttons feel superb under the fingers, it's super quiet (unless you want it to be loud), and it looks phenomenal. As well as all of this, those frosty temps mean you can shove up the wattage if you want, or just have a ton of headroom to avoid throttling in the future. I would really struggle to want to spend over $1,000 on any gaming handheld right now, but if I were flush with cash, I would be majorly tempted to pop the X20 in my basket. If you already have the Xbox Ally X, I wouldn't recommend spending another $1,300 to get a better screen, thermals and TMR sticks (plus some little extras). If, however, you're deciding between the two, I can say that the new additions are very welcome and make for a refined, desirable device. If you've got the cash to splash, it's a sweet device. It's just a shame that the memory crisis has killed handheld market prices. 3. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs. sources.title: WWE 2K26 is collaborating with Capcom for a DLC pack adding five WWE wrestlers as Street Fighter action figures
sources.text: The WWE 2K26 X Street Fighter Elite Pack adds new special moves and cosmetic parts WWE 2K26 is getting a special collaboration DLC pack which sees Street Fighter action figures being added to the game. Mattel first launched its WWE Elite Collection X Street Fighter action figures in 2025, which features WWE superstars dressed as Street Fighter characters. To date, there have been four series of these figures, and now a selection of them are being added to the game as playable characters. They’ll be arriving in the WWE 2K26 X Street Fighter Elite Pack, which will be a separate paid DLC pack not included in any existing bundles or premium editions of the game. The pack, which will be available from October 28, contains playable versions of the five following crossover action figures: Rather than simply reskinned versions of the existing wrestlers, each character will have their own entrance music and video, and will have their own movesets featuring Street Fighter special moves including the Shinku Hadoken, Psycho Crusher, Spiral Arrow, Electric Thunder and Shoryuken. As well as the five superstars, the pack will also include 15 extra create-a-superstar parts from numerous Street Fighter characters, including M. Bison, Ryu, Akuma, Vega and Chun-Li. VGCâs WWE 2K26 review called it the best entry in the series to date, but noted that it didnât innovate too much over the 2K25 edition and still had room for improvement. âWWE 2K26 offers another net gain over its predecessor, ensuring the series continues to evolve in a positive direction,â we said. âWhile its new reversal system will initially divide players and the spectre of microtransactions continues to loom over MyFaction, the overall package introduces more quality-of-life features to ensure each of its numerous modes is better than it was last time.â
